wu: Earth Day Quiz Relay: Teams race to answer 10 quick review questions (e.g., 'Present perfect for experience?', 'Past continuous signal word?') by writing answers on the board. Fastest team gets a point.
wuAlt: Grammar Ball Toss: Students toss a ball and answer a review question when they catch it.
Word Chain Challenge: Teams take turns adding one word to a chain of grammar terms (e.g., 'present → perfect → continuous').
pres: Show 5 eco-rules flashcards (e.g., 'Turn off lights', 'Use reusable bags'). Model: 'We must turn off lights to save energy.' Elicit more rules, then drill sentences with 'must/should'. Check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Video Clip: Play a 1-minute Earth Day video, pause to extract rules as class sentences.
Realia: Show a plastic bottle and a reusable bag, elicit 'We should use reusable bags instead of plastic ones.'
prac: Green Rules Matching: Students match rule halves (e.g., 'We must...' → '...recycle paper') in pairs. Then, play 'Rule Relay'—teams race to write correct full sentences on the board.
pracAlt: Sentence Transformation: Change 'You can litter' to 'You shouldn't litter' in pairs.
Rule Charades: Students act out eco-rules for teammates to guess in sentences.
ls: Earth Day Podcast Listening: Students listen to a 2-minute teen podcast about green habits and tick 3 rules mentioned. Then, in pairs, compare answers and add one more rule they heard.
re: Eco-Simon Says: Teacher calls out commands like 'Simon says turn off the lights!' Students mime the action. Fast-paced to re-energize after break.
prod: Eco-Poster Design: Teams create a 5-rule green poster for the American Space using 'must/should'. They present their poster with 2-minute explanations (e.g., 'We must plant trees because...').
rw: Reading Carousel: Teams rotate through 3 stations—(1) Read a short text about Earth Day history, (2) Match headings to paragraphs, (3) Find 5 'must/should' sentences. Then, write their own 2-sentence rule for the Space.
st: Read 'The Lorax' excerpt, discuss its message. Close with: 'Today we reviewed grammar and made eco-rules—well done! Thank you, class.'
g: Students shoot paper balls into a bin after answering a review question correctly.
Teams race to write correct grammar sentences on the board.
Teams draw eco-rules for others to guess in sentences.
Teams bid on correct sentences, using fake money.
Students stand up and answer quick review questions in turns.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a 'Green Pledge' badge with 3 personal rules using 'must/should'.
Support: Use sentence frames ('We must...') to complete the poster rules.
hw: Design a 5-rule green poster for your home using 'must/should'.
Write 60 words: 'Why Earth Day matters to Morocco'.
Record a 30-second video explaining one eco-rule in English.
tip: Use local context (e.g., 'We should preserve Morocco's beaches') to make grammar relevant and boost engagement.
